title: Continuous metabolic monitoring by interstitial glucose measurement (CGM) in free flaps
summary: In a free flap operation, tissue is transferred together with its blood vessels to another part of the body. During the first days after surgery the blood supply of this tissue can fail and the tissue can die. Today the flap is checked by hand every hour, and circulation problems are often noticed late. In this study, patients receive two small glucose sensors of the type used in diabetes care in addition to usual monitoring: one in the transferred tissue and one on the upper arm for comparison. The study tests whether this measurement works reliably in routine care and whether a drop in tissue glucose can signal circulation problems. Treatment itself is not changed by the study.
conditions: Tissue defects requiring free microvascular tissue transfer; postoperative vascular compromise of free flaps

interventions.name: Arm 1 comprises patients undergoing free microvascular tissue transfer. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Age 18 years or older
- Planned free microvascular tissue transfer (adipocutaneous, myocutaneous or osteocutaneous) with inpatient postoperative monitoring at the study centre
- Suitable cutaneous monitoring window allowing safe sensor placement in the flap
- Written informed consent; for adults unable to consent, written consent of the legal representative under section 1821 German Civil Code, assent of the patient where possible, and own consent obtained on regaining capacity
Exclusion criteria:
- Known severe allergy to sensor components
- Local sensor placement not possible (e.g. marked local infection, no flap exposure, position over the perforator)
- Concurrent participation in an interfering interventional study
- Unacceptable additional risk according to physician judgement
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding
